The fix is PR #1943 (commit `cd6cf1fcbdab85d05529d015dfb911dfef885b84`, ticket O3-6093), "Improve support for arrow functions in expression variable extractor." Falkon links the commit to the PR through its merge commit, and the ticket key appears in the commit message. I did not read the commit's diff, so which lines it changed is inferred from the current code, not confirmed against the patch.

The implementation in esm-core is in `packages/framework/esm-expression-evaluator/src/extractor.ts`:

- `visitArrowFunctionExpression` (lines 111–120) collects the arrow's parameter names into a new `boundNames` set and visits the body with that context. This is what keeps `x` from being reported in `a.map(x => f(b))`, while `f` and `b` are still reported.
- `visitIdentifier` (lines 150–154) only adds a name to `variables` if it is not a global and not in `context.boundNames`.
- `EvaluationContext` (lines 159–164) carries `boundNames`, and `visitExpression` dispatches `ArrowFunctionExpression` to the visitor at lines 68–69.

The regression cases for this behaviour are in `extractor.test.ts` (lines 47–63), including `a.map(x => f(b))` expecting `['a', 'f', 'b']`. The changeset entry is `.changeset/flat-mammals-fail.md`.
